title: Two-factor authentication with an authenticator app (TOTP)
description: TOTP two-factor authentication for server apps: 160-bit secrets with otpauth:// QR URIs, confirm-before-enable enrollment, RFC 6238 verification with a one-step window and replay protection, per-account attempt limits, AES-256-GCM secrets at rest with key rotation, HMAC-peppered one-time recovery codes, step-up checks, a PostgreSQL store and a Fetch adapter.

notes: Requires a TypeScript build and Web Crypto (crypto.subtle HMAC SHA-1/SHA-256 and AES-GCM, getRandomValues), TextEncoder/TextDecoder, btoa/atob and the Fetch Request/Response APIs: Node.js 22+, Bun, Deno, Cloudflare Workers, Next.js route handlers and Hono.
Framework-neutral core; mount the HTTP adapter with your framework's catch-all route.
No runtime packages, environment reads, timers or network activity at install or import time.

parts.use: RFC 6238 TOTP and base32 helpers callable without a store (one file)

configuration: On PostgreSQL, apply schema.sql and use createSqlTwoFactorStore with your query executor; on other databases implement TwoFactorStore with single-statement conditional updates for activate, advanceStep, consumeRecoveryCode and registerAttempt.

Generate a 32-byte AES key from a secret manager and pass it as encryption.keys[<id>] with currentKeyId; to rotate, add a new id, make it current, keep the old id until reencryptSecret has run for every user.
Pass recoveryPepper: at least 32 random bytes from a secret manager, kept separate from the database.
Set issuer to your product name (no colon); the account name is usually the user's email.
After a password sign-in, check isEnabled(userId) and, when true, hold a second-factor-pending session until verify or verifyRecoveryCode succeeds.
Pass authenticatedAt (when the user last proved their password) to disable and regenerateRecoveryCodes; re-prompt for the password when they refuse with reauthentication-required.
For a lockout policy (N consecutive failures lock the account for a fixed time from the Nth) pass lockoutMs; for strict six-digit input pass allowCodeSpaces: false.

Mount createTwoFactorHandler under one prefix with exact allowedOrigins, an authenticate hook that reports the session stage, a rateLimit(key) hook, a trusted clientIp(request) and an onVerified hook that upgrades the session.
limitations: TOTP only (SHA-1, 6 digits, 30 seconds, the settings every major authenticator app supports); no SMS, email codes, WebAuthn or passkeys.
Does not render the QR code (see the qr-code module), store users, manage sessions or verify passwords; the application supplies the session stage and authenticatedAt.
The attempt limit is a fixed window per account (default 5 per 15 minutes); a legitimate user can be locked out by someone who knows their password. Add IP limits through the rateLimit hook.
Comparisons are constant time in JavaScript, but HMAC and AES run in the platform's Web Crypto; recovery-code hashes are looked up by database equality, which is safe because they are keyed HMACs.
Keys and pepper are application-supplied; losing the encryption key makes every enrolled secret unreadable (users then sign in with recovery codes and re-enroll).

The in-memory store is for tests and prototypes only; the SQL store is tested on PostgreSQL semantics through PGlite, which runs as a single connection, not on every hosted Postgres or under real multi-connection contention.
Production database correctness, key management, session handling and consuming-application acceptance remain project responsibilities.
decisions: TOTP only: SHA-1, 6 digits, 30 s, ±1 step, each step once; no SMS or email codes
over the limit → 429; recovery codes HMAC-stored; secrets AES-256-GCM; stale sign-in → 403
options: maxAttempts (5) per attemptWindowMs (15 min) or lockoutMs; stepUpMaxAgeMs (10 min); recoveryCodeCount (10)

verification.command: npm run build && node --test tests/two-factor.test.mjs tests/two-factor-sql.test.mjs
behaviors: totpCode matches the RFC 6238 Appendix B SHA-1 vectors (8 digits and 6-digit truncations); base32 matches RFC 4648
enrollment creates a 160-bit CSPRNG secret in base32 and an otpauth URI with percent-encoded issuer and label
an accountName with a colon is refused with bad-request (JSON 400 over HTTP); user ids containing a colon enroll through the adapter with a colon-free label
2FA is enabled only after a valid code for the pending secret; the pending secret expires and a restart replaces it
verification accepts one step of clock skew either way, rejects two, and fails malformed codes
an accepted time step (including the confirming one) and earlier steps cannot be reused; exactly one of four concurrent verifies wins (memory and PGlite)
five attempts per account per 15 minutes, shared by recovery codes, atomic under concurrency, reset after the window or a success

secrets are stored as AES-256-GCM ciphertext with a key id and user-bound AAD; old keys decrypt after rotation and reencryptSecret moves rows to the current key; the secret is never returned after confirmation
recovery codes are random, stored only as HMAC-SHA-256 with the pepper, single use under concurrency, and regenerate replaces all
disable and regenerateRecoveryCodes refuse without re-authentication in the last 10 minutes

HTTP adapter: enroll, confirm, verify, recovery, regenerate and disable routes; origin check, 401 from authenticate, 403 for settings routes from a second-factor-pending session, 429 from the rateLimit hook and lockout with retry-after, bounded body and cache-control no-store
schema.sql applies and the SQL store passes the core behaviors on PostgreSQL

with lockoutMs, maxAttempts consecutive failures lock the account for lockoutMs from the attempt that reached the limit; attempts while locked are refused without extending it; a success or the end of the lock resets the count; concurrent guesses cannot exceed the limit (memory and PGlite)
with allowCodeSpaces false, codes with spaces fail for verify and enrollment confirmation

changes: Parts entry: the core file's TOTP, base32 and otpauth helpers work without a store.
New options with the 0.1.0 behavior as default: lockoutMs (consecutive-failure lockout) and allowCodeSpaces.

Breaking (SQL): the SQL store writes two_factor_attempts.locked_until, so run the migration below before upgrading. Store: registerAttempt takes an optional lockout argument and AttemptWindow may carry lockedUntil; schema.sql adds two_factor_attempts.locked_until (ALTER TABLE two_factor_attempts ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS locked_until bigint). Custom stores that ignore the argument fail closed in lockout mode (the count never resets except on success).
First release: core, in-memory store, PostgreSQL schema and store, and Fetch adapter.
